data.gender_notes: Harlow is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Named for a field where hares were common. In the Middle Ages, the name Harlowe was used for a place where hares were hunted. The name is derived from the Old English word hære, meaning hare, and law, meaning meadow. The name Harlow carries the meaning “Hare's meadow” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Harlow usually hope their child will grow to embody hare's meadow and live with faith, good character and purpose.

Ultimately, the name Harlow serves as a motivation for us to appreciate the beauty and wonder of God's creation and to live our lives in harmony with nature.
